title: Ubi Kinampay ube (Kinampay): Characteristics
metaDescription: Ubi Kinampay ube is a traditional ube variety from traditional Bohol cultivar. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Ubi Kinampay ube is a traditional ube variety, also sold or known as Kinampay or Bohol ube. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources.

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Ubi Kinampay ube is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Kinampay or Bohol ube, this is the same ube. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ube variety finder](/crop-varieties/ube), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).
Key facts about Ubi Kinampay ube

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources
rows: Kinampay, Bohol ube, Kinampay ube, Quinampay

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ube fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
It is recommended food and processing.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Ube generally takes 8 to 11 months, harvest October to February.
**Fruit:** Red purple to violet flesh, distinct earthy aroma, rich flavor.
**Where:** Bohol (about 35 percent of national ube output comes from the province).
Native to Panglao Island and Guindulman, Bohol.
Ube is traditionally planted May to June, February planting shown possible with DOST dormancy breaking methods.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: bohol's prized ube, called the queen of Philippine yams, UPLB calls it the flavor benchmark and Bohol has applied for Geographical Indication protection. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Ubi Kinampay ube
Processors pay for a deep purple flesh that stays purple when cooked. Pick a registered variety for color and yield, and plant whole small tubers or setts.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Kinampay the same as Ubi Kinampay?
items.a: Yes. Kinampay is another name for Ubi Kinampay. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Ubi Kinampay?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
